Question B-003-018-004.

Why the correct answer is right: An interlock switch removes dangerous high voltage when the cabinet opens, protecting the person accessing the supply.

Per-choice notes:
- sourceIndex 0: "To keep anyone opening the cabinet from getting shocked by dangerous high voltages": This is the correct choice because an interlock switch removes dangerous high voltage when the cabinet opens, protecting the person accessing the supply.
- sourceIndex 1: "To keep dangerous RF radiation from leaking out through an open cabinet": This is a near-miss because it shifts attention from To keep anyone opening the cabinet from getting shocked by dangerous high voltages. In station access, shock hazards, high-voltage rescue, and safe de-energizing before work, it names a different cause, control, component, or safety action than the one required here.
- sourceIndex 2: "To keep dangerous RF radiation from coming in through an open cabinet": This answer would fit a different fault than To keep anyone opening the cabinet from getting shocked by dangerous high voltages. In station access, shock hazards, high-voltage rescue, and safe de-energizing before work, it names a different cause, control, component, or safety action than the one required here.
- sourceIndex 3: "To turn the power supply off when it is not being used": This option confuses another station topic with To keep anyone opening the cabinet from getting shocked by dangerous high voltages. In station access, shock hazards, high-voltage rescue, and safe de-energizing before work, power alone is not the control or safety mechanism being tested in this item.
